hypothesis.title: cart readiness probe failing with 503 'warming up', pods removed from endpoints
hypothesis.summary: The cart service's readiness probe has been failing for ~9 minutes with HTTP 503 status and "warming up" messages. This caused cart pods to be removed from service endpoints. When frontend attempts to call cart, it receives "upstream connect error" because no healthy cart endpoints are available, resulting in 21.5% error rate on frontend. The cart service appears stuck in initialization and unable to become ready.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on frontend 5xx errors spiking from 0.4% to 21.5%. Tracing the error propagation: 100% of failing frontend traces end in cart (traces:frontend:summary shows 44/44 errors originate from cart). The failing trace shows "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection failure" when frontend tries to call cart. The critical evidence is k8s:cart:Unhealthy:0 showing 54 readiness probe failures with HTTP 503, and logs:cart:1 showing cart itself logging "health check /readyz returned 503: warming up" starting 9 minutes before the alert. This means cart pods are failing their readiness probes, being removed from service endpoints, and frontend cannot reach them. The currency and checkout deploys (24m and 28m before alert) are red herrings—they are not on the failing path (traces show errors terminate at cart, not checkout or currency). Cart's own metrics show stable CPU (20%), memory (43%), and low error rate (0.4%), ruling out resource exhaustion, CPU saturation, or memory issues. The probe failure pattern matches RB-probes and the "warming up" message suggests cart is stuck in an initialization state. This is a probe_failure on cart itself.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: Shows 54 readiness probe failures on cart pod with HTTP 503, directly explaining why cart is unreachable from frontend
Cart itself logs 'health check /readyz returned 503: warming up' starting 9m before alert, confirming the service is stuck in initialization
100% of failing frontend traces (44/44) terminate at cart, proving cart is the error origin not just a symptom
Shows the exact failure mode: 'upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: connection failure' when calling cart
4,610 frontend errors calling cart with connection failures, confirming widespread unavailability starting 9m before alert
Cart request rate dropped from 21.9 to 10.3 req/s, consistent with pods being removed from service endpoints due to probe failures

suggested_actions.title: Check cart pod logs for initialization errors
suggested_actions.rationale: Identify why cart is stuck in 'warming up' state and cannot pass readiness checks

suggested_actions.title: Verify cart service endpoints and pod status
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo get endpoints cart && kubectl -n otel-demo get pods -l app=cart
suggested_actions.rationale: Confirm how many cart pods are ready and available in the service endpoint list

suggested_actions.title: Restart cart pods to clear stuck initialization
suggested_actions.rationale: If cart is stuck in a transient initialization state, a restart may clear it and allow pods to become ready

alternatives.why_less_likely: Valkey-cart metrics show healthy request rate (61 req/s), stable latency (3ms p95), and low error rate (0.4%). If valkey-cart were unavailable, we would see its own metrics degrade, but they remain normal.

Checkout deployed 28m before alert, but traces show 100% of errors terminate at cart, not checkout. Frontend also logs only 696 checkout errors vs 4,610 cart errors, and checkout is not on the failing path shown in traces.

retrieved_documents.snippet: ## Summary A payment release changed the shape of the `amount` object. 35% of charges failed with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'units')`. Checkout's error-rate alert fired 9 minutes after rollout. ## Root cause Bad deploy. The new code assumed `amount.units` was always set; older clients sent `amount.nanos` only. ## Resolution `kubectl rollout undo deployment/payment`. …

retrieved_documents.title: Cart / Valkey errors and timeouts
retrieved_documents.snippet: Decide whether the problem is the client pool or the server. - Server: `kubectl -n otel-demo exec deploy/valkey-cart -- valkey-cli --latency` and `SLOWLOG GET 10`. High latency or `BUSY` => datastore degradation. - Client: server latency flat but cart logs `pool busy=N/N` or "timeout awaiting connection" => pool exhaustion. Raise the pool size and restart cart.

retrieved_documents.title: Readiness probe failures
retrieved_documents.snippet: Failing readiness probes remove pods from Service endpoints; callers get 503 / "no healthy upstream". 1. `kubectl -n otel-demo get endpoints <svc>` - fewer addresses than replicas? 2. `kubectl -n otel-demo describe pod <pod>` - look for `Unhealthy` events. 3. Check the probe path and thresholds, and the failedReadinessProbe flag.
